app_caches.what: Caches of classic Teams, Discord, Slack, Spotify (Data) and VS Code.
app_caches.used_for: Rebuilt by each app on next start; Microsoft's own Teams fix deletes the whole Teams folder contents.
app_caches.risk: Slower first start; Teams may ask to sign in again and forget small preferences.
app_caches.catalog_concern: VS Code's caches are in %APPDATA%\Code (Cache, CachedData, CachedExtensionVSIXs), not %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\VSCode, so that part finds nothing.

appdata_autodiscover.what: Any folder under %LOCALAPPDATA%/%APPDATA% (3 levels) whose NAME matches a list (Cache, GPUCache, blob_storage, Crashpad, CacheStorage, BrowserCache...).
appdata_autodiscover.used_for: Most such folders are rebuildable caches, but a name is not proof: some hold crash reports, offline web-app data or whole browser profiles.
appdata_autodiscover.risk: Lost offline web-app data (CacheStorage), unsent crash reports (Crashpad), Electron attachments (blob_storage), or a mis-named profile (CyberGhost's BrowserCache).
appdata_autodiscover.before_cleaning: Close apps first; review the list.
appdata_autodiscover.catalog_concern: Name-based matching offered as safe and pre-selected. The sign-in guard catches IndexedDB/Cookies, but not other data; 'crashpad', 'crash reports', 'cachestorage', 'blob_storage', 'browsercache(s)' should not be safe.

appx_logs.what: Not documented by the vendor. Folders AppxPackages, PackageManagement and RemotePackages under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows.
appx_logs.used_for: Unknown; names suggest package staging or management data.
appx_logs.risk: Unknown contents; possibly package or provider data.

backup_files.what: *.bak/*.old/*.tmp files directly in %windir% and a few app folders, plus Downloaded Program Files.
backup_files.used_for: Leftovers of setups and edits. Downloaded Program Files holds ActiveX controls IE/apps still use.
backup_files.risk: A .bak may be the only copy of an older config; removing ActiveX controls breaks sites/apps that use them (Microsoft KB 4015218).
backup_files.catalog_concern: File-name patterns marked safe; a name does not prove a leftover.

bitlocker_logs.used_for: Logs only, by name; encryption keys are not stored here.

bits_transfers.what: Not documented by the vendor at these paths. The real BITS job queue is qmgr*.dat in ProgramData\Microsoft\Network\Downloader.
bits_transfers.used_for: BITS queues background downloads (Windows Update, Defender, Intune). Microsoft resets it only with BITS stopped.
bits_transfers.risk: If it reaches the queue: in-progress downloads cancelled, possible BITS errors.
bits_transfers.catalog_concern: Marked safe and deletes whole folders with no service stop; the listed paths do not match the documented queue location.

brackets_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Brackets editor 'ext' and 'cache' folders.
brackets_cache.used_for: A cache is rebuilt by the editor; 'ext' may be extension data.

crash_dumps_system.what: Kernel crash dumps (Minidump, LiveKernelReports, MEMORY.DMP) and cluster.log.
crash_dumps_system.used_for: Evidence for diagnosing blue screens, hangs and failover cluster problems.

dbg_logs.what: Not documented by the vendor. %LOCALAPPDATA%\dbg\Logs (debugger logs, by name).

delivery_opt_user.what: Not documented by the vendor. Per-user DeliveryOptimization Cache/Logs folders under %LOCALAPPDATA%.
delivery_opt_user.used_for: Delivery Optimization caches are rebuildable download caches.
delivery_opt_user.catalog_concern: Delivery Optimization's cache is system-wide; this per-user path likely does not exist. Overlaps scan_delivery_optimization_do.

delivery_optimization.what: Delivery Optimization's cache of update and Store downloads shared with other PCs.
delivery_optimization.used_for: Windows clears it itself; deleted content is downloaded again when needed. Disk Cleanup offers it as Delivery Optimization Files.
delivery_optimization.risk: Re-downloads; other PCs on the network cannot fetch those files from this one.
delivery_optimization.catalog_concern: On Windows 10/11 the cache is under ServiceProfiles\NetworkService\...\DeliveryOptimization\Cache; SoftwareDistribution\DeliveryOptimization\Cache likely does not exist.

delivery_optimization_do.what: Delivery Optimization cache and log folders (per-user and ProgramData).
delivery_optimization_do.used_for: Download cache; Windows trims it itself and re-downloads as needed.
delivery_optimization_do.catalog_concern: Overlaps scan_delivery_opt_user; the documented cache path (ServiceProfiles\NetworkService\...) is not listed.

diagnostic_data.what: Diagnostic Data Viewer data and Feedback Hub files.
diagnostic_data.used_for: Viewer data shows what diagnostics were sent; Feedback Hub keeps feedback attachments.
diagnostic_data.risk: Lost viewer history and unsent feedback.

dmf_logs.what: Not documented by the vendor. Log and ETL files in %windir%\Logs\DMF.
dmf_logs.used_for: Diagnostic logs only, as the name and file types show.

dns_cache.what: Nothing: a stub that returns no items. The DNS cache is in memory.
dns_cache.used_for: ipconfig /flushdns clears it; Windows refills it on the next lookups.
dns_cache.catalog_concern: Lists nothing; either implement the flush or remove the entry.

downloads_folder_old.used_for: Things you downloaded: installers, documents, archives. Often the only copy.
downloads_folder_old.risk: Permanent loss of downloaded files you still need.

duplicate_files.what: Groups of files with the same size and the same first and last 8 KB (MD5).
duplicate_files.used_for: A finder; nothing is ticked. Matching only the ends is not proof the files are identical.
duplicate_files.risk: Two different files (VM images, databases, videos) can be reported as duplicates and one deleted.
duplicate_files.before_cleaning: Verify with a full hash before deleting.
duplicate_files.catalog_concern: Docstring says 64 KB, code reads 8 KB; a full-content compare should confirm a duplicate.

empty_folders.what: Empty folders in your user folders and %LOCALAPPDATA%.
empty_folders.used_for: Usually leftovers, but apps create some empty folders on purpose (e.g. a Store app's LocalState, TempState, AC).
empty_folders.risk: An app that expects its folder may fail or reset; little space is gained.
empty_folders.catalog_concern: Rated safe; walking %LOCALAPPDATA% reaches Packages\<app>\ folders Windows created for the package.

etl_logs.what: Windows Update ETL traces, Delivery Optimization logs and Windows\Temp\ScriptArtifacts logs.
etl_logs.used_for: Get-WindowsUpdateLog builds the readable update log from these ETLs.
etl_logs.risk: Update history for troubleshooting is lost.

font_files_temp.what: Not documented by the vendor. LocalService\...\FontDrivers and %TEMP%\Font* folders.
font_files_temp.catalog_concern: The %TEMP%\Font* glob is tested with isdir and never matches; the real font cache folder is ...\Local\FontCache.

game_caches.what: EpicGamesLauncher Data\Portal\Cache; Steam htmlcache Cache, Code Cache and GPUCache leaves (including Default); named Battle.net, EA Desktop, Ubisoft Connect, GOG Galaxy and Discord cache folders.
game_caches.used_for: Cached launcher pages, downloaded interface assets, compiled web code and GPU data. Launchers and Discord recreate these caches as needed; installed games, download staging and account profiles are outside these targets.
game_caches.risk: The next launch may be slower or redownload interface assets. GPU and shader cache rebuilding can cause temporary stutter. Cleaning while a launcher is running can leave locked files or race cache writes.
game_caches.before_cleaning: Close the affected launchers and Discord. Select only caches you intend to rebuild, and allow time for slower first launches and temporary stutter afterwards.

group_policy_logs.what: %windir%\Debug (netlogon.log, PASSWD.LOG, etc.), Group Policy logs and the GroupPolicy Operational .evtx.
group_policy_logs.used_for: Logs for sign-in, domain and Group Policy troubleshooting.
group_policy_logs.risk: Lost domain/policy diagnostics; the .evtx is a live event log held by the Event Log service.
group_policy_logs.catalog_concern: Deleting an .evtx contradicts event_logs being disabled; drop the evtx path.

ide_caches.what: JetBrains caches/index/logs, Visual Studio .vs, ComponentModelCache and Settings, ~vs* temp files, Notepad++\backup, and the whole FileZilla folder.
ide_caches.used_for: JetBrains caches and VS ComponentModelCache are rebuilt. VS Settings holds your IDE settings, Notepad++\backup holds UNSAVED tabs, FileZilla's folder holds saved sites and passwords.
ide_caches.risk: Lost unsaved Notepad++ text, all FileZilla saved servers/passwords, Visual Studio settings; JetBrains logs lost.
ide_caches.catalog_concern: DANGEROUS: %APPDATA%\FileZilla (sitemanager.xml), Notepad++\backup and VisualStudio\<ver>\Settings are user data offered as safe. Keep JetBrains caches/index and ComponentModelCache only.

install_temp.used_for: Used while a feature update installs and briefly for rollback.
install_temp.risk: Breaks an upgrade in progress or a rollback.
install_temp.before_cleaning: Only when no upgrade is pending.
install_temp.catalog_concern: $WINDOWS.~BT/~LS live at the drive root, not in %windir%; Panther\*-ms is a glob tested with isdir and never matches.

iso_vhd_files.what: .iso, .vhd and .vhdx files in your Downloads folder.
iso_vhd_files.used_for: Disk images you downloaded or created; a VHD/VHDX can be a working virtual machine disk.
iso_vhd_files.risk: Losing a VM disk or an image you cannot download again.
iso_vhd_files.before_cleaning: Make sure none is mounted or used by a VM.

large_files.what: Any file over 100 MB in Documents/Desktop/Downloads, %LOCALAPPDATA%, Program Files and Steam\steamapps\common.
large_files.used_for: A finder, not junk: these are your files, installed programs and games. Nothing is ticked.
large_files.risk: Deleting files under Program Files or steamapps breaks programs and games; others are your data.
large_files.catalog_concern: Items under Program Files and steamapps\common should be danger, not caution.

maps_cache.what: Windows Maps' LocalState and a TileDataLayer database.
maps_cache.used_for: Maps' LocalState is app data (favourites, settings); offline maps live in ProgramData\Microsoft\MapData.
maps_cache.catalog_concern: The Packages path is built as %LOCALAPPDATA%\Local\Packages\... with an unexpanded *, so it never matches; if fixed, it would delete a whole LocalState (app data) as safe.

maps_offline_cache.what: Bing Maps app's LocalState: its settings and saved data.
maps_offline_cache.used_for: Offline maps are in ProgramData\Microsoft\MapData; LocalState is app data, not a cache.
maps_offline_cache.before_cleaning: Remove offline maps from Settings > Apps > Offline maps.
maps_offline_cache.catalog_concern: Whole LocalState offered as safe -- the same reason photoscan_cache was disabled.

msi_logs.used_for: Installer logs and Windows Update traces, used for troubleshooting.
msi_logs.catalog_concern: Rated safe; Windows Update ETLs are the source of Get-WindowsUpdateLog. Overlaps scan_etl_logs.

msp_patches.what: EVERY .msp patch in C:\Windows\Installer, referenced or not.
msp_patches.used_for: Windows Installer needs these to repair, patch and uninstall software (Office, SQL, VC++...).
msp_patches.risk: Installed software can no longer be updated, repaired or uninstalled.
msp_patches.catalog_concern: DANGEROUS: no reference check, unlike scan_orphaned_installer_packages. Remove it or reuse that set-difference.

ndis_cache.used_for: By name, network connection data; VPN/dial-up entries are kept in a similar folder (Network\Connections\Pbk).
ndis_cache.risk: Possibly lost VPN or connection settings.
ndis_cache.catalog_concern: A network-connections folder rated safe; NDIS binding cache does not live in a user folder.

network_debug_logs.what: Not documented by the vendor. LogFiles\Nettettl and %LOCALAPPDATA%\...\Network Diagnostics.
network_debug_logs.catalog_concern: 'Nettettl' looks like a typo and matches nothing.

novatrons_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. The whole %APPDATA%\Novatrons folder.
novatrons_cache.used_for: Unknown app; a whole app data folder usually holds settings.
novatrons_cache.risk: Lost settings or data of that app.
novatrons_cache.catalog_concern: Whole app folder offered as safe.

old_av_quarantine.what: Quarantine folders of Avast, AVG, Malwarebytes and Defender.
old_av_quarantine.used_for: Hold detected files in a neutralised form so they can be restored if harmless.
old_av_quarantine.risk: False positives can no longer be restored; the AV's database still lists the items.
old_av_quarantine.before_cleaning: Empty quarantine from the antivirus itself.
old_av_quarantine.catalog_concern: Paths contain 'Avast\ quarantine' (space) and a non-existent Defender path, so it finds nothing.

old_files.what: Files not modified for 6 months in Documents, Desktop, Downloads (not Pictures/Videos).
old_files.used_for: A finder: these are your own documents. Nothing is ticked.
old_files.risk: Permanent loss of real documents; age says nothing about value.

orphaned_installer_packages.what: .msi/.msp files in C:\Windows\Installer that no installed product references.
orphaned_installer_packages.used_for: Unreferenced packages are not used for repair or uninstall. Fails closed if the registry cannot be read.
orphaned_installer_packages.risk: A mis-read registry could orphan a needed package; the product then cannot be repaired or removed.

orphaned_virtual_disks.what: Virtual disks over 1 GB that no installed hypervisor can open.
orphaned_virtual_disks.used_for: Usually left behind by an uninstalled VirtualBox/VMware; nothing uses them now.
orphaned_virtual_disks.risk: The disk may still hold data someone wants.

perflogs.what: C:\PerfLogs (Performance Monitor data-collector output) and LogFiles\WMI\RtTracking.
perflogs.used_for: PerfLogs holds reports an admin chose to record. Not recreated.
perflogs.risk: Lost performance reports someone created on purpose.
perflogs.catalog_concern: Rated safe; these are deliberately collected diagnostics.

powershell_ise_cache.used_for: The scanner's own description says 'saved scripts'; ISE keeps settings elsewhere.
powershell_ise_cache.risk: If it holds scripts, they are lost.

powershell_logs.what: PSReadLine command history, PowerShell transcripts and PowerShell's own logs.
powershell_logs.used_for: History is what the Up arrow recalls; transcripts are audit records an admin or policy turned on.
powershell_logs.risk: Lost command history and audit transcripts (which may be required by policy).
powershell_logs.catalog_concern: Rated safe, but it is user history and audit data. Note PSReadLine lives in %APPDATA%, not %LOCALAPPDATA%, so that part finds nothing today.

powershell_modules_cache.used_for: History is your saved PowerShell commands; modules folder is not a documented PowerShell location.
powershell_modules_cache.catalog_concern: Command history is user data, not a cache; also PSReadLine history is in %APPDATA%, so the listed %LOCALAPPDATA% path matches nothing.

prefetch.what: Windows Prefetch (.pf) files: records of what each program loads at start-up.
prefetch.used_for: Windows uses them to start programs and boot faster, and prunes them itself. Rebuilt as programs run.
prefetch.risk: Next boots and program launches are slower until rebuilt; no space worth gaining.
prefetch.catalog_concern: The scanner marks items safe; the tabs relabel it caution. Deleting Prefetch has no benefit.

print_nightmare_logs.what: spool\PRINTERS and SERVERS (queued jobs) plus spool\drivers: the installed printer drivers.
print_nightmare_logs.used_for: Printers print through the drivers in spool\drivers. They are not recreated.
print_nightmare_logs.risk: Printers stop working and the spooler may fail to start; queued jobs lost.
print_nightmare_logs.catalog_concern: DANGEROUS: spool\drivers holds installed printer drivers. Also no spooler stop check.

print_spooler.used_for: Hold print jobs waiting to print. Deleting cancels them; the standard fix for a stuck queue.
print_spooler.before_cleaning: Stop the Print Spooler service first (the scanner checks).

printer_driver_cache.what: spool\drivers (installed printer drivers) and spool\PRINTERS (queued jobs).
printer_driver_cache.used_for: Printing uses these drivers; not recreated.
printer_driver_cache.catalog_concern: DANGEROUS: same spool\drivers problem as scan_print_nightmare_logs.

recent_files.what: Recent Items shortcuts and the jump-list files (*.automaticDestinations-ms, *.customDestinations-ms).
recent_files.used_for: These ARE the Recent lists, Quick access and the pinned items in taskbar/Start jump lists. Not recreated.
recent_files.risk: Pinned jump-list items and Quick access pins (f01b4d95cf55d32a.automaticDestinations-ms) are lost, and recent-file lists empty. Privacy gain only.
recent_files.before_cleaning: Only if you want your history and pins cleared.
recent_files.catalog_concern: Rated safe, but deleting automaticDestinations removes the user's own pins; it should be caution and unticked.

recycle_bin.what: The Recycle Bin on every drive: your deleted files.
recycle_bin.used_for: Lets you restore deleted files; emptying is permanent.
recycle_bin.risk: Permanent loss of files you may want back.
recycle_bin.catalog_concern: Marked safe and still listed in the Large Items tab, although per_drive_recycle_bin (caution) was meant to replace it.

search_index.what: The Windows Search index database (Windows.edb / Windows.db) and its temp/usage files.
search_index.used_for: Start menu, Explorer and Outlook search use it. Rebuilt by re-indexing, which takes hours.
search_index.risk: Search returns little until re-indexing finishes; files are locked by WSearch.
search_index.before_cleaning: Use Indexing Options > Rebuild instead, or stop WSearch.

store_app_caches.what: Named cache folders inside Store apps' LocalCache (Cache/Temp and WebView2 Cache, Code Cache, GPUCache, shader caches) -- never LocalCache itself.
store_app_caches.used_for: Rebuilt by each app; sign-in data (IndexedDB, Local Storage, Cookies) is left alone.
store_app_caches.risk: Slower first start; a game's 'cache' folder may hold content that is downloaded again.

superseded_app_versions.what: Older version folders of MathWorks Service Host and of Squirrel-updated apps (app-x.y.z beside Update.exe), skipping running ones.
superseded_app_versions.used_for: Squirrel normally removes old versions after an update; leftovers are not used. Service Host rebuilds itself when MATLAB starts.
superseded_app_versions.risk: No rollback to the previous version; a version still in use by another session could break.

sysinternals_logs.what: Not documented by the vendor. The whole Sysinternals folders in %LOCALAPPDATA% and %APPDATA%.
sysinternals_logs.used_for: Sysinternals tools keep most settings in the registry; these folders may hold saved traces or data.
sysinternals_logs.risk: Lost saved traces or tool data.
sysinternals_logs.catalog_concern: Whole app folders offered as safe, against the catalog rule.

triumph_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. The whole %APPDATA%\Triumph folder.
triumph_cache.used_for: Unknown app; whole app data folder.
triumph_cache.catalog_concern: Whole app folder offered as safe.

usb_shadow_copies.what: SYSTEM's CryptnetUrlCache: cached certificate revocation lists and OCSP replies.
usb_shadow_copies.used_for: Windows reuses them to check certificates; deleted entries are fetched again (certutil -urlcache * delete does the same).
usb_shadow_copies.risk: Slightly slower first certificate checks; offline revocation checks fail until refetched.
usb_shadow_copies.catalog_concern: Name and description ('USB shadow copies and ReadyBoost') do not match what it deletes.

userprofile_temp.used_for: Programs' scratch files; leftovers are not needed.
userprofile_temp.risk: A running installer may need its files.

uwp_all_apps_cache.what: Same named Store-app cache folders as scan_store_app_caches.
uwp_all_apps_cache.used_for: Rebuilt by each app; sign-in data is not touched.
uwp_all_apps_cache.catalog_concern: Duplicate of scan_store_app_caches: same bytes counted twice.

virtual_disk_images.what: Virtual disks over 1 GB (.vhd/.vhdx/.vdi/.vmdk/.qcow2) whose hypervisor is installed.
virtual_disk_images.used_for: These are working virtual machines or WSL distributions. Compacting reclaims space; deleting destroys them.
virtual_disk_images.risk: A whole VM or WSL distribution is lost.

virtual_drives.what: Not documented by the vendor. DAEMON Tools ImageCache folders and the whole WinCDEmu folder.
virtual_drives.risk: May hold images you created or tool settings.

winSxS_temp.used_for: Servicing finishes pending file replacements from here at the next restart.
winSxS_temp.risk: An update waiting for a restart can fail or leave Windows inconsistent; Microsoft says never delete inside WinSxS.
winSxS_temp.before_cleaning: Never delete; restart and let Windows clear it.
winSxS_temp.catalog_concern: Offered as caution and listed twice in cleanup_module; anything inside WinSxS should be refused.

windows_app_extensions_cache.used_for: By name, a database of registered app extensions.
windows_app_extensions_cache.risk: Unknown; apps' extensions may stop being found until re-registered.
windows_app_extensions_cache.catalog_concern: A 'database' rated safe with no evidence it rebuilds.

windows_connected_accounts_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\IdentityOLTCache -- by the scanner's own description, cached account tokens.
windows_connected_accounts_cache.used_for: Token caches like IdentityCache/OneAuth keep Office, Teams and Outlook signed in.
windows_connected_accounts_cache.risk: Sign-outs from Microsoft 365 apps and connected accounts.
windows_connected_accounts_cache.catalog_concern: DANGEROUS: a token store offered as safe. Its siblings IdentityCache and OneAuth are in SIGN_IN_STORES; IdentityOLTCache is not.

windows_defender_logs.what: Defender's Logs and Support folders (MPLog, MpSupportFiles.cab) and per-user Scans\History / Quarantine paths.
windows_defender_logs.used_for: Support files are for Microsoft support cases. Quarantine holds detected files you might need to restore.
windows_defender_logs.risk: Lost Defender diagnostics; if quarantine is reached, false positives can no longer be restored.
windows_defender_logs.before_cleaning: Remove quarantine items from Windows Security instead.
windows_defender_logs.catalog_concern: Rated safe. The per-user Defender paths do not exist (Defender keeps them in ProgramData); quarantine should never be a safe item.

windows_inbox_apps_cache.used_for: Path is doubled ('Local\Local') and does not exist; nothing is deleted.
windows_inbox_apps_cache.catalog_concern: Dead path; description (Calculator/Photos/Mail) does not match.

windows_insider_logs.what: Feedback Hub data and log folders.
windows_insider_logs.used_for: Hold feedback attachments and diagnostics waiting to be sent.
windows_insider_logs.risk: Unsent feedback and its diagnostics are lost.

windows_insider_preview_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Windows Insider upgrade staging folders.
windows_insider_preview_cache.used_for: Staging for Insider builds; only needed while a flight installs.
windows_insider_preview_cache.risk: Breaks an Insider upgrade in progress.
windows_insider_preview_cache.before_cleaning: Only when no build is installing.

windows_installer_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. .msi/.msp files in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Installer.
windows_installer_cache.used_for: If these are cached installers, Windows Installer needs them to repair or uninstall.
windows_installer_cache.risk: A product that cannot be repaired or removed.
windows_installer_cache.catalog_concern: Offered with no reference check; scan_orphaned_installer_packages's approach would be safer.

windows_installer_rollback.what: Not documented by the vendor. Folders C:\Windows\Installer\Patch and \001.
windows_installer_rollback.used_for: Anything inside Windows\Installer belongs to Windows Installer's repair/uninstall cache. Rollback during installs uses C:\Config.Msi.
windows_installer_rollback.risk: Software that cannot be repaired, patched or uninstalled.
windows_installer_rollback.catalog_concern: Microsoft says the Windows Installer folder must not be deleted from.

windows_logs.what: CBS, DISM, MoSetup logs, setupapi.*.log and WindowsUpdate.log.
windows_logs.used_for: Diagnostics for updates, upgrades and driver installs (setupapi.dev.log records every device install).
windows_logs.risk: Lost evidence for update, upgrade and driver problems.
windows_logs.before_cleaning: Not while an update or SFC/DISM is running.

windows_old.what: Windows.old: the previous Windows installation left by an upgrade, including old user files.
windows_old.used_for: Lets you go back to the previous version and recover old files. Windows removes it itself after a while.
windows_old.risk: No way back to the previous version; files left in the old profile are lost. Manual deletion often fails on permissions.
windows_old.before_cleaning: Copy anything you need out of it; prefer Storage Sense.

windows_optional_features.used_for: Parts of the component store used by servicing.
windows_optional_features.risk: Microsoft: deleting anything inside WinSxS can stop Windows booting or updating.
windows_optional_features.catalog_concern: InstallTemp is offered as safe; anything inside WinSxS should be refused.

windows_printer_migration_cache.what: spool\PRINTERS: queued print jobs (not printer-migration data).
windows_printer_migration_cache.used_for: Jobs waiting to print; deleting cancels them.
windows_printer_migration_cache.risk: Queued jobs lost; files locked while the spooler runs.
windows_printer_migration_cache.catalog_concern: Duplicate of scan_print_spooler without its spooler check; description wrong.

windows_recovery_env_cache.catalog_concern: Description (WinRE/ReAgentc) is not documented for this folder.

windows_reliability_logs.used_for: Reliability Monitor's data is kept elsewhere (ProgramData\Microsoft\RAC).
windows_reliability_logs.catalog_concern: If pointed at RAC it would erase Reliability history, which should be caution.

windows_shell_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. The whole LocalCache of ShellExperienceHost.
windows_shell_cache.used_for: Shell UI (Start/Action Center) cache, by location.
windows_shell_cache.risk: Unknown; shell UI may reset parts of its state.
windows_shell_cache.catalog_concern: Whole LocalCache, against the app's own rule; target named cache folders.

windows_terminal_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. The whole LocalCache of the Windows Terminal package.
windows_terminal_cache.used_for: Terminal's settings are in LocalState (documented), so LocalCache is probably cache, but its contents are not documented.
windows_terminal_cache.catalog_concern: Offers a whole LocalCache, which the app's own rule (WhatsApp incident) forbids; target named cache folders.

windows_terminal_settings_cache.used_for: This is your Terminal configuration (profiles, colours, keybindings). Not recreated as you had it.
windows_terminal_settings_cache.risk: All Windows Terminal settings reset to default.
windows_terminal_settings_cache.catalog_concern: Settings offered as safe. (Microsoft's unpackaged path is 'Windows Terminal' with a space, so this may not match today.)

wmi_logs.what: WMI logs (wbem\Logs) and wbem\Repository\FS -- part of the WMI repository database.
wmi_logs.used_for: The repository holds every WMI class and registration; Windows and many apps (this one included) depend on it. Not rebuilt by deletion.
wmi_logs.risk: Broken WMI: management tools, Defender, apps and scripts fail. Use winmgmt /salvagerepository instead.
wmi_logs.catalog_concern: DANGEROUS: wbem\Repository\FS is offered as safe. On current Windows the repository files sit directly in wbem\Repository, so it may not match, but it must be removed.
